Commentary.Commentary: Back with the chase! The players of Afghanistan form a huddle before they spread out to take their respective positions. Also, walk out the two openers of Pakistan where Sahibzada Farhan will open the innings alongside Saim Ayub. Allah Mohammad has the new ball in his hands on his debut, and he will start the proceedings. So far, in all three matches before this one, the team batting first has won all the matches. Can Pakistan change that stat, or will Afghanistan manage to defend their total of 169? Let's find out.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Pakistan’s response with the ball was mixed. While Shaheen Afridi was economical, the likes of Haris and Nawaz went the distance. Faheem Ashraf, however, was the standout - breaking the big partnership and removing both set batters before chipping in with wickets of Azmatullah Omarzai and Mohammad Nabi to finish with figures of 4 for 27. His late strikes ensured Pakistan stayed in the contest. Now, with 170 to chase, it all comes down to how Pakistan handle the Afghan spinners. The Powerplay will be crucial if they are to stay in control of this chase. The chase is about to begin, so don’t go anywhere.

The man of the moment, Ibrahim Zadran of Afghanistan, is up for a quick chat. He says that they were just trying to keep things simple. Adds that he had a good partnership with Sediqullah Atal in the last game and went with the same game plan. Mentions that he has been working on his game and trying to rotate the strike more and target one bowler at a time. Says that it is a good wicket, but he reckons they are 10-15 runs short. Ends by saying that they will look to make that up with some good bowling and fielding.

The innings didn’t start brightly for Afghanistan, as Rahmanullah Gurbaz fell early to Saim Ayub in the second over. But Atal and Zadran steadied the ship with a classy partnership, mixing aggression with composure. They punished the loose balls, especially targeting Haris Rauf and Sufiyan Muqeem, who leaked plenty of runs. Both batters looked in complete control, racing to fifties and keeping the scoreboard moving at a healthy rate. The partnership not only repaired the early setback but also put Pakistan under immense pressure as the bowlers struggled to find breakthroughs.

Afghanistan have posted a strong total of 169 for 5, giving themselves a solid chance in this Tri-Series clash at Sharjah. After choosing to bat, their innings was defined by a superb 113-run stand between Sediqullah Atal and Ibrahim Zadran, both bringing up fluent half-centuries. Pakistan did manage to fight back late in the innings, courtesy of Faheem Ashraf’s brilliant spell at the death, where he claimed four wickets and restricted Afghanistan from pushing past 180. Still, 169 looks like a competitive score, especially with Afghanistan’s spin-heavy attack waiting to come into play.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! Afghanistan players are in a huddle, and Allah Mohammad receives his maiden T20I cap from skipper Rashid Khan. The two umpires make their way out to the middle, followed by the Pakistan team, who take up their respective field positions. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Sediqullah Atal are the two openers for the Afghans. Shaheen Afridi has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Before we start the game, the players from both sides, the match officials, and the fans present at the ground stand united in solemn silence, observing a minute’s tribute to honor the victims of the devastating earthquake in Afghanistan and the floods in Pakistan, remembering all those affected by these heartbreaking tragedies.

PITCH REPORT - Ramiz Raja is pitchside. He says that it is a brand new pitch. Adds that the sheen is gone, and the batters are finding it easy to score runs square of the wicket, but it also has something for the spinners as the game goes on. Aamer Sohail joins him and says that it is very different from how it used to be. Tells that the pacers are getting some extra bounce and pace, and the ball is coming onto the bat nicely. Adds that he is a bit surprised with the bowlers because the wicket has the juices, and he expects the fast bowlers to do well in this game with different variations. Says that this is the second time this pitch will be used, and it will act better, and the batters will get an advantage. Raja ends by saying that a change of pace will be crucial in this game.

The skipper of Pakistan, Salman Agha, says that they wanted to chase today, especially after seeing the heavy dew yesterday. Confirms that Shaheen Afridi and Haris Rauf are back in the XI, with Hasan Ali and Salman Mirza missing out. Admits that Afghanistan have quality spinners and their mystery bowlers are world-class, so Pakistan will need to be careful and play them smartly.

The skipper of Afghanistan, Rashid Khan, says that they will bat first. Adds that runs on the board in Sharjah is important as it becomes a bit difficult to bat later on. Mentions that dew factor could be a concern later on, making it harder to grip the ball, but they just have to play good cricket. Says that they are confident after their victory last night and reckons they do not have a total in mind, and will try to adjust according to the conditions. Informs that Mujeeb Ur Rahman and Sharafuddin Ashraf, who was the Man of the Match against UAE, are not playing. Allah Mohammad is making his T20I debut, and Noor Ahmad is also back in the side.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Sahibzada Farhan, Saim Ayub, Fakhar Zaman, Salman Agha (C), Hasan Nawaz, Mohammad Nawaz, Mohammad Haris (WK), Faheem Ashraf, Shaheen Afridi (In place of Hasan Ali), Haris Rauf (In place of Salman Mirza), and Sufiyan Muqeem.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Sediqullah Atal, Darwish Rasooli, Karim Janat, Azmatullah Omarzai, Rashid Khan (C), Mohammad Nabi, Allah Mohammad (On T20I Debut) (In place of Sharafuddin Ashraf), Noor Ahmad (In place of Mujeeb Ur Rahman), and Fazalhaq Farooqi.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favour of Afghanistan, and they have elected to BAT first.

Building on the last paragraph, England’s batting was nothing short of a lacklustre performance, crumbling for a mere 131 runs in just 24.3 overs. The innings was a tale of woe, with only Jamie Smith showing any resistance with a knock of 54. However, he received no support from the rest of the lineup. A flurry of wickets saw England collapse from 102/4 to 131 all out, with seven batsmen failing to reach double figures. Joe Root, Harry Brook, and Jos Buttler all got starts but failed to convert them, and the team has had a collective batting failure. Now, with just a paltry target of 132 to chase, South Africa will be brimming with confidence and fancy their chances of an easy victory. A straightforward chase would see them take a commanding 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series.

Meanwhile, in the first ODI between South Africa and England in Leeds, South Africa’s bowlers delivered a dominant performance after choosing to field first. Wiaan Mulder was destructive, claiming 3 wickets for 33 runs, including the key scalp of opener Jamie Smith. Keshav Maharaj was equally impressive, tearing through England's lower order with a four-wicket haul for just 22 runs, effectively ending the innings. Nandre Burger and Lungi Ngidi also contributed with a wicket each, maintaining tight control and piling pressure on the English batsmen from the outset.

So the stage is set for another fiery clash in Sharjah. Pakistan have momentum and confidence, but Afghanistan have plenty of motivation to get one back over their neighbours. Expect Pakistan’s pace against Afghanistan’s spin to be the key battle again, and the short turnaround could test both teams’ bench strength. With a place in the final up for grabs and bragging rights at stake, this one promises to be a cracking contest. Stay tuned for the toss and team lineups!

For Afghanistan, the opener against Pakistan exposed the old problem - not converting good starts with bat or ball. Rahmanullah Gurbaz’s fireworks and Rashid Khan’s late blitz kept the margin respectable, but their seamers leaked heavily at the death. They responded well against the UAE, though, with youngsters Ibrahim Zadran and Sediqullah Atal scoring fluent fifties to set up a strong total, before Sharafuddin Ashraf and Rashid spun their way through the middle overs to seal a comfortable win. Rashid also etched his name into the record books, overtaking Tim Southee as the leading wicket-taker in T20Is. Still, Afghanistan will know their top order needs more consistency, and their fast bowlers must hold nerve at the back end if they are to challenge Pakistan here. Additionally, to keep a note here, they are playing this match within 24 hours after their last match yesterday, so players will need to manage fatigue and mental stiffness.

Pakistan’s campaign so far has been built on depth and balance. In the first game, skipper Salman Agha led from the front with a classy half-century, before Haris Rauf and Shaheen Afridi dismantled Afghanistan’s chase with pace and precision. In the second, against the UAE, it was the youngsters who stole the show, where Saim Ayub’s dazzling 69 and Hasan Nawaz’s 56 powered them past 200, while Hasan Ali, Mohammad Nawaz, and even Ayub with the ball ensured that Asif Khan’s fireworks didn’t derail their plans. What’s noticeable is how Pakistan have managed to win games even while rotating their big guns like Shaheen and Rauf, a sign of a confident squad with depth. With no major injuries reported, they look well placed to not just secure the final spot tonight but also can test different combinations.

Hello and welcome to the Sharjah Cricket Stadium for the 4th match of the UAE T20I Tri-Series, where Pakistan take on Afghanistan less than 24 hours after the first round wrapped up. It’s the start of the second and decisive leg, and both sides come into this with contrasting moods. Pakistan, under Salman Agha’s leadership, have been the team to beat - two wins out of two, sitting pretty at the top with four points and needing just one more win to confirm their place in the final. Afghanistan, meanwhile, bounced back strongly against the UAE after a tough loss to the same Pakistan side in the opener, and find themselves second on the table with two points.
... MATCH DAY ...

The reverse leg of the Tri-Series in the UAE is ready to kick off at the iconic Sharjah Cricket Ground. First on the card, a rerun of the series opener as Afghanistan square off with Pakistan in Match 4, a clash that promises even more intensity this time around. Pakistan come in riding a wave of confidence, having delivered exactly what was expected from the most experienced side in this competition - two convincing wins, and a strong grip on the table. In both outings so far, Pakistan have won the toss, chosen to bat and turned tricky Sharjah conditions into a platform for dominance. On a surface that often plays a touch on the slower side, they have stacked up 182 and 207, imposing first innings scores that set the tone. In the opener, skipper Salman Agha led the way with a classy fifty. In the second, Saim Ayub and Hasan Nawaz stepped up with half-centuries of their own. Throughout both games, the middle order kept the innings moving with handy contributions that ensured Pakistan never lost momentum. However, win or lose, there is still plenty of room for improvement in the bowling department. Conceding 50 or more during the fielding restrictions in both games has been a concern, and this is an area they will want to tighten up quickly. One big positive for them was that even without their premier pacers Haris Rauf and Shaheen Afridi, the next line of relatively younger and less experienced quicks showed good courage and control. The question now is whether the senior pair will return to the eleven for this match. Afghanistan come into this contest on the back of a commanding win over the United Arab Emirates, with barely any time to catch their breath. Rashid Khan’s side saw contributions right through the batting order, as different players rose to the occasion at crucial stages. Even so, they will be hoping for a stronger show from their star opener Rahmanullah Gurbaz, who has looked a little out of rhythm. The opening stands are yet to cross 20, but Sediqullah Atal has impressed at the top while Ibrahim has started to find his touch. With the ball, their spin unit has kept things exceptionally tight, with skipper Rashid Khan taking charge alongside Mujeeb and the rest of the supporting cast including Sharafuddin Ashraf. The need of the hour is for their pace attack to challenge a side like Pakistan where they leaked a lot of runs in the series opener. Notably, the new-ball phase has proved to be a bit more challenging to deal with. But once the ball loses its shine, batting becomes relatively easier, especially with wickets in hand. Three matches so far, all three won by the side setting the target. That bracket of 160-190 looks just enough to restrict the chasing side. Will that trend change this time around? A win takes Pakistan straight to the final whereas an Afghan triumph tightens the contest even more. With objectives pretty clear in both camps, it sets up for a crucial clash between the fierce Asian rivals.
